name: SmallClaw

overview_markdown:
SmallClaw is a local-first AI agent framework from Xpose Market, positioned as an open-source alternative to cloud AI assistants. It is chat-first: a single-pass LLM call decides whether to respond conversationally or invoke tools, avoiding the separate planning/execution/verification agent loops that small models handle poorly. This design choice directly targets users running Ollama, llama.cpp, or LM Studio on consumer hardware, with optional hybrid support for OpenAI API and Codex OAuth.

Feature-wise it is surprisingly complete for its size: line-precise file editing, multi-provider web search (Tavily, Google, Brave, DuckDuckGo), Playwright-powered browser automation, terminal access, persistent session memory with pinned context, and a drop-in SKILL.md skills system. Recent commits show active development through v1.1, including security hardening, Docker improvements, background tasks, sub-agents, a Telegram file browser, MCP/webhook support, and a task system with dark mode UI.

Compared to OpenClaw, SmallClaw trades ecosystem breadth for simplicity and latency. It lacks OpenClaw's multi-channel messaging surface and massive skills registry, but its single-pass architecture is arguably better suited to weak local models. Caveats: no official GitHub releases, an ambiguous license ('All rights reserved' in the description despite an open-source claim), and essentially no genuine community discussion found in search results.
